newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak foreign minister resigns, cites poll chaos.
newsitem.headline: Slovak foreign minister resigns, cites poll chaos.

text.p: Slovak Foreign Minister Pavol Hamzik resigned on Monday saying the domestic political situation and a failed weekend referendum had made his position untenable.

"Contemporary political events in Slovakia, especially the circumstances surrounding the referendum on Slovakia's NATO membership and the election of the president have to the greatest possible extent narrowed the scope for me as foreign minister to pursue the foreign policy priorities of our nation," Hamzik said in a statement.

"With my resigntion I want to signal primarily to Slovakia that the foreign minister cannot effectively seek to realise his goals in a situation when everything, including vital international interests of Slovakia, is subordinated to domestic fights for power," Hamzik added.

He was referring to a political feud between President Michal Kovac and Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar which contributed to a fiasco that scuttled referendums on NATO membership and direct election of the president at the weekend.
"During the time when I headed the foreign ministry I did all I could to serve Slovakia to the maximum. I am convinced that I could do no more under the circumstances," Hamzik said.
Hamzik, a career diplomat who became foreign minister last August, had for a long time been seen as ardent defender of the Meciar government.
